headline: Simile raises $200M at $2B valuation just 5 months after Series A
summary: The synthetic-user startup, founded by a Stanford PhD, secured a massive Series B round led by Greenoaks.
details: Simile has announced a $200 million Series B funding round, valuing the company at $2 billion. This significant achievement comes just five months after the startup raised $100 million in its Series A.

The Series B round was led by Greenoaks, with participation from existing investors like Index Ventures, as well as new backers including Hanabi, Bain Capital Ventures, A*, Factory, Definition, and CVS Health Ventures.

Founded by Stanford PhD graduate Joon Sung Park, Simile offers simulated users for market research and product development. Park's prior work includes a project called "Smallville," where AI agents simulated human lives.

The startup's ambitious mission is to accurately simulate all eight billion people on Earth. While this goal is incredibly complex due to human unpredictability, the core service of simulating users for research is seen as a promising area.
Simile operates in a growing market, with other startups like Aaru also attracting significant VC attention, having raised a Series A at a $1 billion valuation in December.
caption:
Simile, a startup creating simulated users for market research, has secured a $200M Series B at a $2B valuation.

Simile has announced a $200 million Series B funding round, valuing the company at $2 billion. This significant achievement comes just five months after the startup raised $100 million in its Series A.

The Series B round was led by Greenoaks, with participation from existing investors like Index Ventures, as well as new backers including Hanabi, Bain Capital Ventures, A*, Factory, Definition, and CVS Health Ventures.

Founded by Stanford PhD graduate Joon Sung Park, Simile offers simulated users for market research and product development. Park's prior work includes a project called "Smallville," where AI agents simulated human lives.

The startup's ambitious mission is to accurately simulate all eight billion people on Earth. While this goal is incredibly complex due to human unpredictability, the core service of simulating users for research is seen as a promising area.

Simile operates in a growing market, with other startups like Aaru also attracting significant VC attention, having raised a Series A at a $1 billion valuation in December.
